output.title: Rounding claims in a one-person business
output.body:
If you run a one-person business, the real question is not whether AI can “handle claims.” It is whether the rounding work is repetitive enough to be treated as a bounded workflow instead of a pile of one-off judgment calls.

That gives you a simple decision rule. Keep it manual if each case needs fresh context or exceptions. Consider support only if the same checks happen again and again. In that setup, AI can sort, compare, or flag items for your review. Final approval stays with you. No system should sign off on your money or liability.

The useful next step is to map one week of the current process. Write down the trigger, the inputs, the decision rule, where rounding happens, and where you stop to check by hand. Then mark which parts are truly repeatable. If the rule can be written down clearly, it is a candidate for support. If it depends on judgment every time, manual review is still the right default.

That is the filter: not “Can AI do it?” but “Which part is stable enough to standardise without giving up owner control?”
